items.title: Divergent nitrous oxide accounting can distort crop carbon intensity scores and agricultural trade
items.abstract: Methods for estimating nitrous oxide emissions, a major contributor to the carbon intensity of nitrogen fertilizer-dependent crops, can produce substantially different results across frameworks. Standardized approaches are needed to avoid distorting trade and strengthen incentives for mitigation of emissions.

items.title: Wheat resilience under compound stress
items.abstract: Compound hot–dry–windy events are becoming more frequent and increasingly damaging to wheat yields in China’s wheat belt, underscoring the need for improved crop management, breeding and climate adaptation.

items.title: Wheat yield sensitivity to compound hot–dry–windy events is increasing in China
items.abstract: Increasing hot–dry–windy events threaten wheat yields in China, with significant yield losses linked to high-temperature, low-humidity conditions. Analysis of extensive yield and climate data reveals worsening sensitivity trends, emphasizing the need for adaptive strategies in agricultural practices.

items.title: When conflict with industrial fishing threatens coastal communities
items.abstract: We developed a global index to identify small-scale fishing communities that are most vulnerable to conflict with industrial fleets. Areas with highest vulnerability, where fishing supports many livelihoods and essential needs, were found to be concentrated in Africa and Asia. Our results highlight priorities for equitable fisheries governance.

items.title: Selective extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using deep eutectic solvents
items.abstract: In this study, the development of an ultrasound method for extraction of phenolic compounds from barley waste using acidic deep eutectic solvents (UAE-DES) was investigated. Optimization of the extraction parameters, which include extraction time, temperature, and ultrasound power (UP), was performed using the One-Factor-at-a-Time (OFAT) experimental design, followed by HPLC-PDA for determination of total quantified phenolic content (TQPC). In addition, the influence of water addition on TQPC was evaluated. The Maximum TQPC obtained was 5.78 mg/g using ChCl: formic acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 30 min, 80% UP, 10% water), and 4.67 mg/g, using ChCl: tartaric acid at a molar ratio (1:2) and optimal conditions of (70 °C, 25 min, 100% UP, and 20% water). The obtained TQPC was 5- and 4-fold higher in comparison with 70% methanol and 70% ethanol extraction. LC–MS-qTOF analysis of DES extracts revealed diverse phenolic compounds, while the concentration range of compounds obtained was as follows: ferulic acid (0.86–2.47 mg/g), catechin (0.12–2.16 mg/g), p-coumaric acid (0.12–0.32 mg/g), naringenin (0.54–0.86 mg/g), and apigenin (0.15–0.91 mg/g). SEM analysis confirmed enhanced accessibility of lignocellulose in DES-treated samples. The sustainability of UAE-DES extraction was assessed using AGREE, AGREEprep, CACI, BAGI, and CaFRI green tools. The grade assessment of each tool resulted in scores: 0.63 for AGREE, 0.57 for AGREEprep, 65 for CACI, 82.5 for BAGI, and 72 for CaFRI, indicating a greener extraction performance of UAE-DES in comparison with …

items.title: The assessment of gastric myoelectrical activity between different stomach regions based on three-channel electrogastrogram signals: a pilot study
items.abstract: IntroductionPrevious studies have widely used surface electrogastrogram (EGG) signals to non-invasively evaluate gastric motility. However, it focused only on the assessment of electrical activity in a certain stomach region and lacked the analysis of interactions between different gastric regions. In the study, we aimed to assess the correlations of myoelectrical activity between distinct stomach areas using functional connectivity (FC) methods by three-channel EGG for the first time.MethodsThe study contained 20 healthy subjects and the dataset for each subject consisted of two three-channel EGG signals (labeled as CH1, CH2 and CH3; CH1 projected onto the region of lesser curvature, CH3 projected onto the region of greater curvature, and CH2 positioned the region between CH1 and CH3) with a sampling rate of 2 Hz acquired from three locations of stomach during a 20-minute period of fasting and postprandial states respectively. Firstly, the EGG signals were band-pass filtered into three slow wave (SW) bands by finite impulse response (FIR) filter, namely bradygastria (0.017-0.033 Hz), normogastria (0.033-0.067 Hz) and tachygastria (0.067-0.15 Hz). Secondly, we employed four FC algorithms (i.e. Spearman correlation coefficient (SCC), phase lag index (PLI), mutual information (MI) and coherence (Coh)) to calculate the connection strength of each pair of gastric areas. Finally, the FC strength between fasting and postprandial conditions for all subjects or the normal weight (NW) or overweight (OW) people and between the NW and OW groups for both fasting and postprandial states…

items.title: Quality evaluation of a traditional Chinese medicine compound preparation containing Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius
items.abstract: ObjectiveWe aim to improve the quality control of Rhodiola rosea, Astragalus membranaceus, and Carthamus tinctorius capsules (RAC capsule) from the aspects of thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC), respectively, and the established quality control methods are suitable for their popularization and application in large-scale production.MethodsA TLC method was established for the identification of R. rosea, A. membranaceus, and C. tinctorius in RAC capsules. A HPLC method with gradient elution and UV detection was established for simultaneous determination of salidroside, tyrosol, hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA), anhydrosafflor yellow B (ASYB), and rhodiolin.ResultsThe TLC chromatograms showed distinct and reproducible spots for the RAC capsule samples at positions consistent with those of the corresponding reference crude drugs, while no interfering spots were observed in the negative control samples. The HPLC method demonstrated excellent linearity (R2 > 0.9991) for all five analytes within their respective concentration ranges with precision, stability, and repeatability; RSDs all below 2%; and average recoveries ranging from 95.07% to 105.61%.ConclusionThe developed TLC and HPLC methods are specific, accurate, and robust, providing a reliable quality control strategy for RAC capsules. The study supports the standardization of this herbal capsule formulation and establishes a foundation for further pharmacological research and clinical investigations.

items.title: Complementary techniques for investigating the molecular dynamics of uncrystallized water
items.abstract: Uncrystallized water (UCW) refers to the fraction of water in hydrated materials that remains uncrystallized upon cooling. Rather than forming bulk ice, this water retains molecular mobility even below the nominal freezing point. In polymers and proteins, UCW includes strongly bound water associated with specific functional groups and more weakly confined water residing in nanoscale environments. As a result, it plays an important role in mechanical behavior, structural stability, and biological function. Because UCW is heterogeneous, no single technique can fully capture its properties, and multiple complementary methods are required. This review highlights how dielectric spectroscopy (DS), nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), neutron scattering, particularly quasielastic neutron scattering (QENS), and terahertz and infrared spectroscopies each probe different aspects of UCW across distinct time and different sample sizes. We outline what each technique measures, the models commonly used to interpret the data, and how combining these approaches helps distinguish between “free,” “bound,” and “non-freezable” water. Studies that apply multiple methods to the same samples, with consistent control of hydration and temperature, are essential for developing a coherent and quantitative picture of UCW. This integrated approach is also key to translating UCW behavior into practical design principles for cryopreservation, pharmaceutical freezing, and biomaterials. Importantly, complementarity arises from differences in timescale and the distinct …

items.title: CRDS-Unet: channel-reversed depthwise separable U-net for efficient tomato leaf disease segmentation
items.abstract: IntroductionAutomated plant leaf disease segmentation is crucial for accurate disease diagnosis and quantitative lesion assessment in precision agriculture. U-Net-based architectures are widely employed for this task, although their high computational complexity sometimes hinders their application in resource-constrained agricultural settings.MethodsThis work investigates depthwise separable convolutions in conjunction with a channel-reversed U-Net for tomato leaf disease segmentation. The channel-reversed encoder allocates more feature channels to the shallow layers and progressively fewer to the deeper layers, the reverse of a conventional U-Net’s channel schedule, with the aim of preserving spatial detail while reducing computation in the deeper, more computationally expensive stages. Depthwise separable convolutions are used throughout the encoder, bottleneck, and decoder to further reduce trainable parameters. The model was trained on lesion masks and evaluated on an independent, held-out subset of the PlantVillage tomato leaf dataset using Dice coefficient, IoU, precision, recall, and F1-score, following a corrected data-splitting protocol that eliminates train/test leakage present in an earlier version of this work.ResultsThe proposed method reduced trainable parameters by over 97% relative to a conventional U-Net (0.96 million versus 31.06 million), at a measured reduction in segmentation accuracy under the training budget evaluated (Dice coefficient 0.79 versus 0.90 for standard U-Net). A supplementary experiment with a longer training budget narrowed this gap subs…

items.title: Culturable bacterial diversity in a recirculating aquaculture system for sole fish farming: analysis of potential pathogens and putative bioremediation, probiotic and antimicrobial significance
items.abstract: Understanding the bacterial diversity present in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) is essential for identifying potential pathogens and taxa with bioremediation and biotechnological relevance, particularly as these artificial environments remain largely unexplored bioresources with untapped microbial potential. This study is the first to characterize the culturable bacterial diversity within a RAS for sole farming (Solea senegalensis) in Portugal, providing a comprehensive first insight into what seems to be a complex bacterial dynamic. Phylogenetic analysis of 193 strains, revealed that Pseudomonadota (76.4%) was the most abundant phylum, followed by Actinomycetia (10.7%), and Bacteroidota (9.8%). At the class level, Gammaproteobacteria (65.7%), Actinomycetia (10.7%), and Alphaproteobacteria (10.7%) dominated, with Alteromonadales (33.9%) and Vibrionales (13.7%) as the prevalent orders. A comparison with metagenomic studies previously reported for similar RAS systems showed some overlap in dominant phyla, however, different genera were also cultivated in the present study, particularly those from the orders Micrococcales and Vibrionales. In all, a total of 48 bacterial genera were identified, with 33 cultivated only from the RAS and 9 cultivated only from its water supply. Our findings reveal the presence of taxa closely related to bacterial strains previously reported for their biotechnological potential, including strains described as probiotics, as producers of antimicrobial compounds, and as agents of bioremediation. items.title: Assessment of probiotic characteristics of lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditional foods of Southern India for preparation of sauerkraut
items.abstract: Probiotics are highly essential for a healthy gut in order to maintain optimum microbial balance, fight against pathogenic bacteria, improve digestion and maintain overall intestinal health. The present investigation was carried out to evaluate the probiotic properties of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) isolated from traditional fermented foods of Southern India. The isolates cultures were tested for acid production using titratable acidity, and six maximum acid-producing (g/L) isolates (DFRM9 11.0, DFRM8 10.0, DFRA9 10.0, DFRD4 10.0, DFRY4 8.0 and DFRD11 7.0) were selected for further analysis. Acid tolerance, bile tolerance, tolerance to the gastrointestinal tract, antibacterial activity, and antibiotic susceptibility, were tested on the above LAB isolates and isolates obtained earlier such as Bifidobacterium bifidum NCDC229, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum DFR4, Pediococcusacidilactici DFR1 obtained during previous studies in our laboratory. Analysis of variance (ANOVA) indicated that Limosilactobacillus fermentum DFRM9 had significantly (p < 0.05) higher probiotic effects among the tested isolates. L.fermentum DFRM9 was used as a starting culture for sauerkraut preparation, and its fermentation activity was compared with that of spontaneous fermentation. The developed functional food was found to have desirable physico-chemical and microbial quality. The results obtained in the present investigation support the use of lacto-fermentation for the production of sauerkraut and indicate the potential of lactic acid bacteria isolated from traditional foods as probiotics in various p…

items.abstract: A battery material can look perfect in the lab and still fail in a real battery. That is the puzzle facing researchers working on solid electrolytes, the materials seen as key to safer, longer-lasting batteries.

items.title: SynFit guides enzyme engineering by balancing several useful traits at once
items.abstract: Enzymes are biology's tiny chemists. They help build, break and rearrange molecules quickly and precisely. In the lab, scientists have long put enzymes to work making useful chemicals. But nature's enzymes cannot do every reaction a researcher might want. Sometimes scientists need an enzyme to take on a job it did not evolve to do. That's where enzyme engineering comes in—researchers make changes to an enzyme, test how those changes affect what the enzyme does and look for versions that work better.

items.title: Paired DNA strands recognize shape, not just sequence, in new small-molecule sensing method
items.abstract: You have probably performed a sandwich assay before, even if you didn't know it. Sandwich assays are the molecular sensing technology behind lateral flow tests like the at-home COVID test. After a sample is dripped onto the test strip, it combines with detector antibodies attached to tiny gold particles, which bind to any viral proteins present. When the sample reaches the test line, a second antibody anchored to the strip binds to a different site on the viral protein, creating a molecular "sandwich." As the gold particles accumulate, the test line turns dark red, becoming visible to the naked eye.

items.title: A sweeter future? AI helps scientists discover new sugar substitutes
items.abstract: Researchers Dr. Shayma El-Atawneh and professor Amiram Goldblum at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem have developed a new computational framework that identified 92 promising candidates for future sugar substitutes from more than 50 million chemical compounds. The study, published in the journal Food Chemistry, demonstrates how artificial intelligence and molecular modeling could accelerate the discovery of new sweeteners while helping overcome one of the industry's persistent challenges: unwanted bitter aftertastes.

items.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

items.title: Scientists discover why a 100-year-old mushroom disease won't go away
items.abstract: Scientists have uncovered a surprising secret behind a mushroom disease that has frustrated growers for more than a century: It involves more than 17 species of harmful bacteria, not just one. The discovery could explain why treatments have struggled to stop the disease and open the door to more effective, eco-friendly solutions.

items.title: The “glue” holding your cells together has a surprising second job
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that E-cadherin, a protein best known as the “glue” holding cells and tissues together, has a surprising second job: helping epithelial cells swallow nearby dead cells. Using live zebrafish and mouse embryos, researchers found that cells can dramatically reshape their lower surfaces to engulf cellular debris while keeping their upper surfaces stable, allowing protective barriers to remain sealed.

items.title: Scientists find evidence for two origins of life on Earth
items.abstract: Scientists probing life’s deepest origins have uncovered evidence that the first free-living cells may have emerged not once, but twice. The findings suggest a striking possibility: life may share one ancient genetic code, yet have undergone two separate transitions into free-living existence.

items.title: For decades, we were told to avoid full-fat dairy. New research says otherwise
items.abstract: Full-fat dairy may not be the health villain it has long been portrayed as, according to a new study finding that three daily servings did not worsen weight, cholesterol, or insulin resistance over 12 weeks. Researchers also observed improvements in blood pressure and nutrient intake, raising questions about longstanding recommendations to choose low-fat dairy.

items.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover a “natural Ozempic” with a surprising advantage
items.abstract: Stanford researchers have discovered an AI-identified natural molecule that dramatically suppresses appetite and promotes fat loss in animals, potentially offering an Ozempic-like weight-loss treatment without common digestive side effects or significant muscle loss. Called BRP, the molecule reduced food intake by up to 50% and targets a different brain pathway, raising hopes for a more precise obesity treatment if future human trials prove successful.

items.title: Scientists discover new Alzheimer’s drug that repairs DNA damage and reduces brain inflammation
items.abstract: Scientists have discovered that a drug originally developed for spinal cord injuries can tackle several key features of Alzheimer’s disease, including DNA damage and inflammation. Already tested for initial safety in humans, the experimental treatment could offer a faster path toward therapies that target the disease at its roots.

items.title: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
items.abstract: Scientists are calling for a major rethink of how we manage high blood pressure, suggesting that eating more potassium could be just as important as cutting back on salt. A new report finds that combining increased potassium intake with reduced sodium consumption may offer greater benefits for blood pressure control than sodium reduction alone.

items.title: Impact of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum UBLP-40 intervention on iron status indicators in iron-deficient women of reproductive age: a double-blind, randomized controlled trial
items.abstract: IntroductionIron deficiency remains highly prevalent among women of reproductive age due to increased physiological demands, inadequate dietary intake, and poor absorption. Conventional iron supplementation has shown limited success in addressing this issue. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum UBLP-40 (Lp40) on iron status indicators in iron-deficient women of reproductive age.MethodsIn this double-blind, randomized controlled trial, 152 iron-deficient women were randomized to receive either a probiotic-iron-ascorbic acid combination (Lp40-Fe-AA, n = 51), iron-ascorbic acid (Fe-AA, n = 50), or probiotic-iron (Lp40-Fe, n = 51) supplement in capsule form once daily, 1 hour before a meal for 12 weeks. Serum ferritin and other iron markers were measured at baseline, week 6, and week 12. Data were analyzed using a generalized linear mixed-effects model.ResultsA significant time-by-group interaction was found for inflammation-adjusted ferritin levels (p = 0.048). In post-hoc analysis, the Lp40-Fe-AA group showed significant improvement in serum ferritin compared to the Fe-AA group (10.33 ng/mL, 95% CI: 7.09–13.57 vs. 4.80 ng/mL, 95% CI: 1.93–7.66; p = 0.014) at 12 weeks. Ferritin levels did not show any significant difference when other groups were compared (Lp40-Fe-AA vs. Lp40-Fe, p = 0.485 and Lp40-Fe vs. Fe-AA, p = 0.076). No significant time-by-group interaction was however observed for hemoglobin, hepcidin, transferrin saturation, and reticulocyte indices.ConclusionThe results of this study indicate that L. plantarum UBLP-40 may offer a m…

items.title: Potential roles of food-derived bioactive peptides in osteoporosis through the gut-bone axis
items.abstract: Osteoporosis is a systemic skeletal disorder characterized by reduced bone mass, microarchitectural deterioration, and increased fracture risk. However, long-term use of current pharmacological therapies is often associated with adverse effects, underscoring the urgent need for safer and more sustainable intervention strategies. Food-derived bioactive peptides have attracted increasing attention because of their potential anti-osteoporotic effects and natural origin. Upon intestinal entry, these peptides may modulate the gut microbiota and its metabolites, improve immune-inflammatory responses, and maintain intestinal homeostasis, thereby influencing bone homeostasis. The gut-bone axis, as a key bidirectional regulatory network connecting the gut microenvironment and bone metabolism, provides a new research perspective for understanding the potential link between food-derived bioactive peptides and bone health. This review systematically summarizes the potential mechanisms by which food-derived bioactive peptides exert bone-protective effects through regulation of the gut-bone axis. Furthermore, we discuss current research progress, remaining challenges, and future directions, with the aim of providing a theoretical foundation for the development of peptide-based intervention strategies against osteoporosis. Given that the current evidence is mainly derived from in vitro and animal studies, the actual effects of food-derived bioactive peptides on osteoporosis still need to be further validated through clinical studies.

items.title: Opportunities and limitations of image analysis-based microplastic quantification and characterization in a hydrological context
items.abstract: Precise characterization of microplastic morphology and size distribution is essential for understanding particle mobility through porous media, since particle size and morphology strongly influence filtration, retention, and transport behavior. Image analysis has been investigated as a cost-effective and efficient way to quantify and measure polydisperse environmental microplastics, but it has yet to be proven effective for use in hydrological studies. In this study, three common image-analysis workflows were evaluated to quantify concentrations and size distributions of Nile Red-stained microplastics in laboratory transport studies. Filter images were captured using (1) a digital single-lens reflex camera; or (2) a stereomicroscope, both as random frames or as stitched full-filter images. Automated particle counts were compared to manual counts from various dilutions, based on panoramic full-filter images. Then, a controlled sand column experiment was conducted as proof-of-concept to evaluate method performance under advective transport conditions. All imaging approaches exhibited concentration-dependent sensitivity, with high particle densities causing quantification and sizing errors due to particle overlap (coincidence) and fluorescence halo effects. Stitched full-filter stereomicroscopic images were deemed too time-consuming for use in high-throughput hydrological studies, but DSLR photography and random frame-stereomicroscopy identified comparable breakthrough timing and mobility trends. Differences in particle recovery and relative concentration magnitudes were driv…

items.title: Phosphorus in Balance: Evaluating the Costs and Benefits of a Circular Economy Approach
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive cost-benefit analysis of producing alternative phosphorus (P) fertilizers from recycled water treatment residuals (Fe-WTR) and cowshed effluents. The cost-benefit values of Fe-WTR are compared to the net costs of recycling P using a synthetic adsorbent (commonly used practice-layered double hydroxide, P-LDH) and the costs of commercial fertilizers. Dairy wastewater is used as a source of P. The cost of 1 ton P using the Fe-WTR process is €329. In contrast, synthetic adsorbents (P-LDH) incur significantly higher costs, amounting to €3329 per ton, underscoring the economic advantage of utilizing waste-derived materials. Adopting Fe-WTR fertilizer not only offers substantial cost savings by avoiding landfill fees (€40 per ton) and wastewater discharge fines (€500 per ton) but also reduces environmental impacts when compared to the use of commercial P fertilizers (non-recycled P). The Fe-WTR method mitigates eutrophication and pollution, presenting the dual benefit of cost-effectiveness and environmental protection, which exceeds the common P recycling practice (LDH). Our conclusions are based on production processes in Israel and compared to previous cost estimations at the world level, assessing the potential gain from such circular production of P globally. Recycling P from waste streams can be economically viable and environmentally preferable at small and large economic scales, supporting global sustainability goals.
items.authors: H. E. Ganem, I. Zohar, M. Litaor et al.

items.title: The impact of alternative recycled and synthetic phosphorus sources on plant growth and responses, soil interactions and sustainable agriculture - lettuce (Lactuca sativa) as a case model.
items.abstract: This research assesses the efficacy of two phosphorus (P) adsorbents as alternative fertilizers in promoting lettuce growth. A synthetic Mg/Al-layered double hydroxide (LDH) and an iron-based recycled water treatment residual (Fe-WTR), both enriched with P from dairy wastewater and added at three dosage levels. We hypothesized that the adsorbents' physicochemical nature will overshadow the biological efforts in the plant ecosystem to increase P solubility, impacting plant growth, nutritional composition, and metabolite profiles. Fe-WTR significantly enhanced lettuce biomass compared to LDH. Yet, elemental analysis revealed higher or equal P concentrations in the low-biomass LDH plants relative to other treatments. Phosphorus uptake appears to influence the assimilation of other nutrients that divided into two groups: calcium, magnesium, zinc, and copper with notable correlations to P and nitrogen, iron, aluminum, vanadium and manganese with low correlations to P. Conversely, P retained poor correlation with most metabolites whereas iron showed a higher correlation with numerous metabolites. Analysis of metabolites, encompassing carbohydrates, the Krebs cycle, amino acids, nucleic acids, and stress and regulatory pathways, revealed diminished levels in the LDH treatments. Overall, carbon assimilation (plant growth) was more effectively predicted by soil P availability (adsorbent type and dose) rather than by cellular P concentration, suggesting root signaling was at play, influencing carbohydrate translocation to the roots. items.title: Biogeochemical impacts on soil phosphorus and other macro- and micro elements solubility, ratios and forms during heatwaves
items.abstract: Increased frequency and amplitude of extreme heat events can affect soil temperature, and biogeochemical processes. High temperatures may have contradicting geochemical and biological effects on essential elements solubility and forms. Endothermic behavior of minerals and oxides results in decreased solubility with increased temperature, while bio-mineralization is stimulated in response to high temperature. To elucidate heatwave impacts on soil biogeochemical processes, we performed a controlled soil incubation experiment and a field survey. Wet and dry alluvial soil sets were incubated at background temperature (33°C) for two weeks and then, a sequence of three heat events was induced (41°C/33°C alternations, five days each) followed by two short events of extreme heat (48°C for two days). Most soil indices changed trends after about 25-30 days. At the first part of the period, P, Al, Fe appeared to reflect endothermic behavior of (hydr)oxides and minerals in the dry soil (i.e., sorbed P was likely dependent on Fe (hydr)oxides dissolution), while trends of Fe/Al in the wet soil followed the dissolved organic C trend. Phosphatases enzymatic activities fluctuated positively with temperature, emphasizing the activity of residual extracellular enzymes sorbed to soil particles (dry soil) in addition to living cells excreted enzymes (wet soil). items.title: New Analytical Approach to Quinolizidine Alkaloids and Their Assumed Biosynthesis Pathways in Lupin Seeds
items.abstract: Alkaloids play an essential role in protecting plants against herbivores. Humans can also benefit from the pharmacological effects of these compounds. Plants produce an immense variety of structurally different alkaloids, including quinolizidine alkaloids, a group of bi-, tri-, and tetracyclic compounds produced by Lupinus species. Various lupin species produce different alkaloid profiles. To study the composition of quinolizidine alkaloids in lupin seeds, we collected 31 populations of two wild species native to Israel, L. pilosus and L. palaestinus, and analyzed their quinolizidine alkaloid contents. Our goal was to study the alkaloid profiles of these two wild species to better understand the challenges and prospective uses of wild lupins. We compared their profiles with those of other commercial and wild lupin species. To this end, a straightforward method for extracting alkaloids from seeds and determining the quinolizidine alkaloid profile by LC–MS/MS was developed and validated in-house. For the quantification of quinolizidine alkaloids, 15 analytical reference standards were used. We used GC–MS to verify and cross-reference the identity of certain alkaloids for which no analytical standards were available. The results enabled further exploration of quinolizidine alkaloid biosynthesis. We reviewed and re-analyzed the suggested quinolizidine alkaloid biosynthesis pathway, including the relationship between the amino acid precursor l-lysine and the different quinolizidine alkaloids occurring in seeds of lupin species. items.title: Valorization of Local Legumes and Nuts as Key Components of the Mediterranean Diet
items.abstract: Legumes and nuts are components of high importance in the diet of many countries, mainly those in the Mediterranean region. They are also very versatile and culturally diverse foods found all over the world, acting as a basic protein source in certain countries. Their genetic diversity is needed to sustain the food supply and security for humans and livestock, especially because of the current loss of habitats, species, and genetic diversity worldwide, but also because of the ever present need to feed the increasing human population. Even though both legumes and nuts are considered as high-protein food and environmentally friendly crops, developed countries have lower consumption rates when compared to Asia or Africa. With a view to increasing the consumption of legumes and nuts, the objective of this review is to present the advantages on the use of autochthonous varieties from different countries around the world, thus providing a boost to the local market in the area. The consumption of these varieties could be helped by their use in ready-to-eat foods (RTE), which are now on the rise thanks to today’s fast-paced lifestyles and the search for more nutritious and sustainable foods. The versatility of legumes and nuts covers a wide range of possibilities through their use in plant-based dairy analogues, providing alternative-protein and maximal amounts of nutrients and bioactive compounds, potential plant-based flours for bakery and pasta, and added-value traditional RTE meals. items.title: The effect of simulation training on the counseling skills of nutritional science students in dietetic internships
items.abstract: Simulations are a common tool in training aircrews, medical personnel and educators, providing experience in scenarios from the relevant content area and expanding the range of responses that simulation participants can acquire before they enter the field. Simulations have also been used in dietetic internships to improve clinical counseling skills. However, the use of structured simulations that involve progressive, multisession patient interactions has not been extensively studied in the context of dietetic internships. This study employed consecutive scenario models where interns developed ongoing interactions with the same simulated patient over multiple sessions, representing a significant methodological innovation in the field. A mixed method methodology was used to analyze closed and open-ended questionnaires which were administered to twenty-one interns, simulation actors and professional dietitians. This pilot study demonstrates the effectiveness of group and individual simulation training in enhancing dietetic interns’ counseling skills during their training and describes how simulation can contribute to both the professional skills and self-efficacy required to lead a counseling session. These findings will enable additional academic departments to examine the integration of simulation into the training programs of interns in tracks that include a practicum.

items.title: The Anticonvulsant Effects of Different Cannabis Extracts in a Zebrafish Model of Epilepsy
items.abstract: Epilepsy is a widespread neurological disorder that remains a critical global public health challenge. While numerous antiepileptic drugs (AEDs) are available, many patients either fail to achieve adequate seizure control or experience significant side effects. One promising alternative is pure cannabidiol (CBD), but using a whole cannabis extract may be equally effective and preferred for some patients. In the current study, we employed the pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced hyperactivity model in zebrafish to compare the effects of CBD with various cannabis extracts. We evaluated three cannabis strains, each subjected to three different extraction methods, and benchmarked the results against the commercially available AED valproic acid (VPA). Our findings revealed that 5.7 µg/mL of CBD and 10 µg/mL of different extracts significantly reduced movement compared to PTZ and VPA. In addition, effective extracts produced effects similar to pure CBD despite containing much lower molecule levels. These results reinforced and expanded previous evidence supporting the clinical potential of both CBD and whole cannabis extracts for seizure control while suggesting a possible entourage effect. Further research is necessary to determine which patients may benefit more from pure CBD versus those who might prefer whole cannabis extracts.

items.title: Physiological Impacts of Energy Drink Consumption: A Clinical Analysis in Adolescents
items.abstract: Energy drink (ED) consumption among Israeli-Arab adolescents is widespread. This study aimed to investigate the acute glycemic and insulin effects of EDs in healthy adolescents. Seventy-one Israeli-Arab adolescents (56% girls, average age 16.04 ± 1.03 years) participated in a non-randomized, case-controlled, open-label study. Participants consumed ED (n = 36) or a volume- and carbohydrate-matched non-caffeinated soft drink (SD, n = 35), followed by a 2 h glucose tolerance test. Blood glucose was measured at baseline and 15, 30, 60, and 120 min post-consumption (T0, T15, T30, T60 and T120, respectively). Serum insulin concentration and caffeine relative intensity were determined 45 min post-consumption (T45). Blood glucose levels peaked significantly at T15 and remained significantly higher at T30 in the ED group compared to the SD group (p = 0.005, p = 0.017, respectively). Insulin concentrations were substantially higher at T45 in the ED group (t [64] = 2.794, p = 0.001). This pattern was especially prominent in heavy ED consumers. A positive correlation emerged between the amount of caffeine consumed (mg/kg), blood glucose levels at T15 and T30, and insulin concentration at T45. This study is the first to demonstrate the glycemic and insulin responses to ED consumption in adolescents, suggesting that regulatory measures limiting ED sales to adolescents could improve their health.

items.title: Disrupted gut harmony in attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder: Dysbiosis and decreased short-chain fatty acids
items.abstract: Background Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) is a prevalent neurodevelopmental disorder with complex genetic and environmental underpinnings. Emerging evidence suggests a significant role of gut microbiota in ADHD pathophysiology. This study investigates variations in gut microbiota composition and Short-Chain Fatty Acid (SCFA) profiles between children and adolescents with ADHD and healthy controls. Methods The study included 42 ADHD patients and 31 healthy controls, aged 6–18 years. Fecal samples were analyzed for microbial composition using 16S rRNA gene sequencing and for SCFA profiles through gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). The study assessed both α and β diversity of gut microbiota and quantified various SCFAs to compare between the groups. Results ADHD subjects demonstrated significantly reduced gut microbiota diversity, as indicated by lower α-diversity indices (Shannon index, Observed species, Faith PD index) and a trend towards significance in β-diversity (Weighted UniFrac). Notably, the ADHD group exhibited significantly lower levels of key SCFAs, including acetic, propionic, isobutyric, isovaleric, and valeric acids, highlighting a distinct microbial and metabolic profile in these individuals. Conclusion This study uncovers significant alterations in gut microbiota and SCFA profiles in children with ADHD, compared to healthy controls. The observed changes in SCFAs, known for their associations with other behavioral and neurologic pathologies, and for their role in neural signaling.
